Travis Head

Where it began

He was born in Adelaide on 29 December 1993 and grew up in Craigmore, in the city's northern suburbs, playing junior cricket for the local club and for Trinity College. He played for South Australia at under-17 and under-19 level and made his Sheffield Shield debut at 18, early in 2012.

At 21 he was made captain of South Australia, the youngest in the state's long first-class history. He led them to a Shield final and was named the competition's player of the year for 2015–16.

The player

He first played Test cricket against Pakistan on 7 October 2018, receiving his baggy green from Nathan Lyon. His first Test hundred, 161, came against Sri Lanka a few months later. By October 2026 he had played 69 Tests and made 4,808 runs at 42.93, with 13 hundreds and 20 fifties. His best by then was 175 against West Indies in Adelaide.

Two summers stand out. In 2023 he made 163 in the World Test Championship final at The Oval and was player of the match as Australia won the title. In the 2025–26 Ashes he moved up to open, reached one hundred in only 69 balls and finished the series as its leading scorer, with 629 runs and three centuries.

What made him special

He scores quickly, and he does not wait for permission. Bowlers who think they have him tied down tend to find the ball heading for the fence. He wins the big moments too: player of the match in a Test final and a World Cup final in the same year is a rare double.

As a young man he had a soft spot for the nineties. He reached them five times in first-class cricket before he finally got to a hundred, after 17 scores of 50 or more. He has been making up for lost time ever since.

Away from the middle

He won the Allan Border Medal, Australia's top cricket award, in 2025 and again in 2026, and the Compton–Miller Medal as player of the 2021–22 Ashes. He has also captained Australia in Twenty20 cricket and served as Test vice-captain. Off the field he follows Port Adelaide in the AFL.

And finally

He is a part-time off-spinner, and he took his first Test wickets in Galle in 2022 with figures of 4 for 10. Plenty of full-time spinners would settle for an afternoon like that.
